notes.summary: Moments describe the shape of a distribution. The first central moment is always zero, the second is the variance, the third measures skewness and the fourth measures kurtosis (peakedness). Expect formula-based questions on Karl Pearson, Bowley, β₁ and β₂.

concepts.title: Moments
concepts.body:
• Raw moments about origin/A: μ'r = Σ(x − A)r/n.
  • Central moments (about mean): μr = Σ(x − x̄)r/n. μ1 = 0, μ2 = variance.
  • Conversion: μ2 = μ'2 − μ'1²; μ3 = μ'3 − 3μ'2μ'1 + 2μ'1³.

concepts.title: Skewness
concepts.body:
• Positive skew: long right tail, Mean > Median > Mode. Negative skew: long left tail, Mean < Median < Mode.
  • Karl Pearson: Sk = (Mean − Mode)/σ, or 3(Mean − Median)/σ. Usually lies between −3 and +3.
  • Bowley (quartile): Sk = (Q3 + Q1 − 2Q2)/(Q3 − Q1); lies between −1 and +1.
  • Moment measure: β1 = μ3²/μ2³, γ1 = μ3/σ³ (sign gives direction).

varieties.name: Raw and central moments
varieties.how: Convert raw moments to central moments with the standard formulas.

example.q: μ'1 = 1, μ'2 = 5, μ'3 = 10 (about A). Find μ3.

varieties.name: Coefficient of skewness
varieties.how: Use Karl Pearson with mean/mode/SD, Bowley with quartiles, β₁ with moments.

example.q: Mean = 45, median = 42, SD = 9. Find Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness.

varieties.name: Kurtosis
varieties.how: Compute β₂ = μ₄/μ₂² and compare with 3.

example.q: μ2 = 2, μ4 = 18. What is the shape?

tips: For a symmetric distribution all odd central moments are zero.
β₁ is always ≥ 0, so use the sign of μ₃ to tell the direction of skewness.
traps: β₁ cannot show negative skewness; γ₁ or μ₃ can.
Bowley's coefficient is bounded by ±1, Karl Pearson's usually by ±3.
μ₂ is the variance, not the SD.

questions.q: The first central moment (about the mean) of any distribution is always:
questions.solution: μ<sub>1</sub> = Σ(x − x̄)/n = 0, because positive and negative deviations from the mean cancel out.

questions.q: Mean = 60, mode = 55 and SD = 10. Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness is:
Q<sub>1</sub> = 20, median = 30 and Q<sub>3</sub> = 50. Bowley's coefficient of skewness is:
For a distribution μ<sub>2</sub> = 4 and μ<sub>4</sub> = 48. The distribution is:
questions.solution: β<sub>2</sub> = μ<sub>4</sub>/μ<sub>2</sub>² = 48/16 = 3. β<sub>2</sub> = 3 means mesokurtic (same peakedness as the normal curve).

questions.q: The first two moments about the value 5 are 2 and 20. The standard deviation is:
questions.solution:
μ2 = μ'2 − (μ'1)² = 20 − 2² = 16.
SD = √16 = 4. (Variance does not depend on the point about which raw moments are taken.)

questions.q: For a distribution μ<sub>2</sub> = 4 and μ<sub>3</sub> = −8. Then β<sub>1</sub> and the direction of skewness are:
questions.solution:
β1 = μ3²/μ2³ = 64/64 = 1.
β1 is always positive; the sign of μ3 (negative) shows the skewness is negative. (γ1 = μ3/σ³ = −8/8 = −1.)
